s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court?
x: M. Fathima Beevi (1989) was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer and Pratibha Patil the first woman President.

s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
x: Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President.

s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the (undivided) Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the undivided AP Assembly in 2004. Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister (UP), and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor (UP).

s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
x: Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman INC president; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman president.

s: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian State?
x: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of the United Provinces in 1947; Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman CM (UP, 1963).

s: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1917)?
x: Annie Besant was the first woman INC President (1917); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (1925).

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson.

s: Who was the first woman President of India?
x: Pratibha Patil, the 12th President (2007-12), was India's first woman President.

s: Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman Chief Minister of which State in 1963?
x: Sucheta Kripalani became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1963, the first woman CM of an Indian State.

s: Who was the first woman IPS officer of India?
x: Kiran Bedi was India's first woman IPS officer.

s: What is the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats under Article 243D(3)?
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the duration of reservations in local bodies?
o: Women's reservation has no such sunset provision, whereas SC/ST reservation is linked to the Article 334 period.
All local-body reservations are permanently fixed by the 73rd Amendment.
SC/ST reservation has no constitutional time limit, but women's reservation ends in 2030.
Women's reservation and SC/ST reservation both automatically end in 2030.
x: Women's reservation in local bodies has no equivalent sunset provision. SC/ST reservation is linked to Article 334, whose current period extends to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.

s: Which of the following provision–subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 334A – Rotation of women's reserved seats after delimitation
Article 243D(2) – Sub-reservation for SC/ST women within SC/ST seats
Article 243D(3) – Rotation of women's reserved seats after delimitation
x: Article 243D(3) reserves one-third of directly elected Panchayat seats for women; rotation after delimitation is Article 334A.

s: When did the Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, which gave one-third reservation for women in Panchayats, come into force?
x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day. The other dates are not its commencement date.

s: What percentage of seats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh local bodies?
x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies.

s: Which of the following is correct about the constitutional one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?
o: A floor that States may raise
A ceiling that States cannot exceed
x: One-third is a floor, not a ceiling; States may raise it, and several provide one-half.

s: Which was the first State to raise the reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions to 50%, and in which year?
x: Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006. Many States followed, and 19 States/UTs now give 50%, including Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are not the first.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation?
o: Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women's reservation.
Half reservation for women in local bodies exists in 19 States and UTs.
Half reservation for women in local bodies is constitutionally mandatory in every State.
In legislatures, one-third reservation is to operate only after delimitation.
x: The constitutional floor is one-third; half reservation exists only in 19 States and UTs that chose it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation in local bodies?
o: SC/ST reservation of seats and chairperson offices is proportionate to population.
Reservation for backward classes is constitutionally compulsory in every State.
Chairperson offices are reserved as provided by State law and allotted by rotation.
Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women's reservation.
x: Reservation for backward classes in local bodies is left to the States; it is not compulsory everywhere.

s: Which Article reserves at least one-third of Chairperson offices in Panchayats for women?
x: 243D(4) covers women chairpersons; 243D(3) covers women's seats and 243T(4) is the municipal provision.

s: What is the minimum age to contest elections to Panchayats and Municipalities?
x: Under Articles 243F and 243V the minimum age is 21, not 25.

s: How many States/UTs now provide 50% reservation for women in local bodies?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (23 (21 States and 2 UTs)); it is added as option 5.
the app's figure 19 — now 21 States and 2 UTs (web: static.pib.gov.in MoPR Highlights, National Panchayati Raj Day 24 Apr 2026)
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (April 2026) counts 21 States and 2 UTs (23) with 50% reservation for women in panchayats; 19 was an older count, and 12, 25 and 9 are wrong.

s: Which Article provides for reservation of seats for STs in Municipalities?
x: ST seats in municipalities fall under 243T(1); 243T(3) and 243T(4) cover women's seats and chairs.

s: What is the position of reservation for Backward Classes in Panchayats under the 73rd Amendment?
x: BC reservation in local bodies is optional and left to the States.

s:
Consider the following statements about reservation in Panchayats:
1. Women's reservation has no sunset clause.
2. SC/ST reservation is tied to Article 334 and runs to 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: women's local quota has no sunset, while SC/ST reservation follows Article 334 to 2030 (104th Amendment).

s: Under Article 243D(2), what share of the seats reserved for SCs and STs in a Panchayat must be reserved for SC/ST women?
x: Article 243D(2) reserves not less than one-third of the SC/ST seats for SC/ST women, not 50%.

s: Women form about what share of representatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions (2026)?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (About 50% (49.75%)); it is added as option 5.
about 46% earlier — now 49.75% (web: static.pib.gov.in MoPR Highlights, National Panchayati Raj Day 24 Apr 2026)
Women are 49.75% – nearly half – of the 25 lakh+ elected panchayat representatives (MoPR, April 2026); 46% was the 2015 figure.

s: What share of reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies did Andhra Pradesh approve in 2026?
x: In 2026 AP approved 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33.33% in urban bodies.

s: Within seats reserved for SCs and STs in Panchayats, what is the minimum share reserved for SC/ST women?
x: Article 243D(2) reserves not less than one-third of SC/ST seats for SC/ST women, not 50%.

s: What was India's Global Gender Gap Index rank in 2018?
x: India was ranked 108th among 149 countries in the 2018 Global Gender Gap Index.

s: The Gender Development Index primarily measures the ratio of female to male achievement in which of the following dimensions?
o: Economic participation, educational attainment, health and political empowerment
Reproductive health, political empowerment and labour market participation
Health, education and command over economic resources
x: GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.

s: Which index uses a 0-to-1 scale on which 1 denotes the worst position for women?
x: This loss scale belongs to the GII; the GDI is read as female-to-male parity, with a value near 1 indicating parity.

s: Which of the following indicators is included under the reproductive health dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Mean years of schooling and earned income
Share of women in parliamentary seats only
x: The reproductive health dimension of GII includes maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.

s: Who publishes the Global Gender Gap Index?
x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.

s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four sub-indices of the Global Gender Gap Index?
x: The four GGGI sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Reproductive Health is associated with GII.

s: What mainly pulls India's Gender Inequality Index position below its overall Human Development Index rank?
o: Low female labour-force participation and low political representation
High female labour-force participation and high political representation
Low male literacy and high maternal mortality alone
High educational enrolment and low life expectancy of men
x: India's GII position is pulled down especially by low female labour-force participation and low political representation.

s: What was India's parity in economic participation in the 2023 Global Gender Gap Index?
x: India's economic participation parity was only 36.7% in 2023, while enrolment parity was achieved at all levels.

s: What was India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index 2025?
x: India ranked 131st of 148 in 2025; 127th was 2023, 129th 2024 and 135th 2022.

s: Which country topped the Global Gender Gap Index 2025 for the 16th year?
x: Iceland was first in 2025, for the 16th year.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about gender indices?
o: The GDI is published by the UNDP
The GGGI is published by the World Economic Forum
In the GII, 1 denotes the worst position
Reproductive health is a dimension of the GGGI
x: Reproductive health is a dimension of the UNDP's GII, not of the WEF's GGGI.

s: What was India's rank in the Gender Inequality Index in the Human Development Report 2025?
x: India ranked 102nd (108th earlier), pulled down by low female labour force participation and representation.

s: Since which year has the World Economic Forum published the Global Gender Gap Index?
x: The WEF has published the Global Gender Gap Index since 2006.

s: What was India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index 2023?
x: India was 127th of 146 in 2023, up from 135th in 2022.

s: The Women, Peace and Security Index is published by the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security together with which institution?
x: The WPS Index is published by the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security and PRIO.

s: What was India's rank in the Women, Peace and Security Index 2025/26?
x: India was ranked 131st of 181 countries in the WPS Index 2025/26; Denmark was first.

s: Which Articles of the Constitution provide for equal franchise in the context of women voters?
x: Articles 325 and 326 provide the constitutional basis for equal electoral franchise.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: It provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
It provides one-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
It includes one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
It provides reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha.
x: The Act does not provide reservation in the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment provides the women's quota in the Lok Sabha?
x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 332A the State Assemblies, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly and 334A commencement and duration.

s: By what name is the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 also known?
x: The 106th Amendment Act, 2023, the women's reservation law, is called the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.

s: Which of the following pairs (body — Article on women's reservation) is correctly matched?
x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 243D covers Panchayats, 243T Municipalities and 332A State Assemblies.

s: Which Article provides for women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the NCT of Delhi?
x: Delhi is covered by Article 239AA(2)(ba), not 332A; it covers directly elected and SC seats since Delhi has no ST seats.

s: Which of the following is NOT provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: An OBC or BC sub-quota within the women's reservation
One-third reservation in the Delhi Legislative Assembly
Rotation of reserved seats after delimitation
One-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies
x: The Act does not provide an OBC or BC sub-quota. It provides reservation in the specified legislatures and provides for rotation after delimitation.

s: Women’s groups demanded the removal of which condition attached to women’s legislative reservation?
o: The condition of reservation only in urban local bodies
The condition of approval by all State Legislatures
The condition of prior approval by the Election Commission
x: Women's groups demand removal of the Census-delimitation condition. Under Article 334A the quota starts only after the first Census after the Act and the delimitation that follows, so it cannot begin before 2034.

s: Which Articles of the Constitution enable women to contest elections to Parliament and State Legislatures?
x: Articles 84 and 173 let women contest; Articles 325 and 326 give equal franchise.

s:
Arrange the following developments relating to women's reservation in chronological order:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) Act enacted
B. 108th Amendment Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha
C. 81st Amendment Bill introduced
D. 108th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha
x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.

s: As which Bill was the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 introduced in Parliament?
x: The 2023 Bill was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and enacted as the 106th Amendment Act.

s: Which government introduced the 81st Constitution Amendment Bill on women's reservation in 1996?
x: The 81st Amendment Bill of 1996 came under the Deve Gowda government and lapsed.

s: When did the Rajya Sabha pass the 108th Constitution Amendment Bill on women's reservation?
x: The 108th Bill passed the Rajya Sabha on 9 March 2010 and lapsed in 2014.

s: For which Assemblies was the women's reservation under the 106th Amendment in force from 17 April 2026?
x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.

s: Why was the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026?
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.

s: When are seats reserved for women to be rotated under Article 334A?
o: Every five years irrespective of delimitation
x: Article 334A provides for rotation of the reserved seats after each delimitation.

s: After delimitation based on which Census will women's reservation under the 106th Amendment begin?
x: The reservation commences only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.

s: For how long is reservation for women provided under the 106th Amendment?
x: The reservation is provided for 15 years and may be extended by Parliament.

s: The proposed 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026 sought to raise the Lok Sabha's strength from 550 to how many seats?
x: The Bill sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats on the basis of the 2011 Census.

s: Which Article ties the start of women's legislative reservation to delimitation after the first Census following the 106th Amendment?
x: Article 334A makes the reservation start only after delimitation on the first Census after the Act, so it is not immediate.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. One-third of SC/ST seats are reserved for women.
2. It provides an OBC sub-quota for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong because there is no OBC sub-quota.

s: On which date did the President give assent to the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
x: Parliament passed the Bill on 21 September 2023 and the President gave assent on 28 September 2023.

s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is which Constitutional Amendment Act?
x: It is the 106th Amendment, reserving 33% of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats for women.

s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam reserves what share of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats for women?
x: The 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) reserves 33% of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats for women.

s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam was piloted by which Ministry?
x: The 106th Amendment came from the Ministry of Law and Justice.

s: Bokkasam Palem, located in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati, is associated with which achievement?
o: It received the first national award for tribal self-governance
It became the first girls’ Panchayat in India
It was ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats
It was the first Panchayat to introduce a BC-women sub-quota
x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.

s: What is a Mahila Sabha?
o: A meeting of women officers of the Election Commission
A statutory committee of the National Commission for Women
A meeting of women members of Parliament before a joint sitting
A women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha
x: Mahila Sabha refers to a women-only meeting conducted before the Gram Sabha, as exemplified in Maharashtra.

s: At least one Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayat is envisaged per which unit?
x: At least one per district is envisaged, providing safe spaces and gender-responsive governance aligned with SHGs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan?
o: It trains Women Elected Representatives in leadership
It has legal-awareness and gender-justice modules
It includes modules on gender-based violence
x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan trains women representatives; sensitising male representatives is Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna.

s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.

s: The Balika Panchayat initiative, India's first of its kind, was launched in June 2022 in which of the following places?
x: The first Balika Panchayat was established in villages of Kutch, Gujarat, in June 2022.

s: The initiative 'Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna' is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Training girls exclusively for urban municipal administration
Providing legal aid only to women prisoners
Increasing women's turnout through electronic voting
x: Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives.

s: The National Commission for Women was set up in 1992 under the NCW Act of which year?
x: NCW was set up in 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990.

s: Which laws are the main legal shield against atrocities and discrimination targeting Dalit and tribal communities?
o: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
x: The safeguards identified are the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

s: According to the findings associated with the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study, women leaders invested more in which of the following?
o: Military infrastructure and border roads exclusively
Goods and facilities requested by women, including drinking water and roads
Only administrative buildings and police infrastructure
x: Women leaders invested more in public goods that women specifically requested, notably drinking water and roads.

s:
Assertion (A): Proxy representation in women-led Panchayats does not legally replace the elected woman.
Reason (R): Proxy representation is an informal exercise of the office by a male relative.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Because proxy representation is only informal, the elected woman is not legally replaced, so R explains A.

s: In which States was the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study (2004) on random reservation of women pradhans based?
x: It studied random pradhan reservation in West Bengal and Rajasthan; women leaders invested more in drinking water and roads.

s: How was the Dalit woman president of Therku Thittai panchayat (Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, 2020) discriminated against?
o: Removed from office by the Collector
Made to sit on the floor at meetings
x: She was made to sit on the floor at meetings and barred from hoisting the flag; the secretary was arrested.

s: What is the practice of a male relative informally running an elected woman sarpanch's office called?
x: Sarpanch-pati is proxy representation; it does not legally replace her and declines in a second term.

s: Which of the following pairs about women's electoral participation is correctly matched?
x: Women first out-voted men in 2019 (and again in 2024). SVEEP is the ECI's programme, the 18th Lok Sabha has 74 women, and AP had 22 women in 2024 (14 in 2019).

s: How many women were elected to the 18th Lok Sabha (2024)?
x: The 18th Lok Sabha has 74 women (13.6%); the 17th had 78, the highest.

s: Which Lok Sabha had the highest number of women members, 78?
x: The 17th Lok Sabha (2019) had 78 women (14.4%), the highest so far.

s: How many women were elected to the 175-member Andhra Pradesh Assembly in 2024?
x: 22 of 175 (13%) were women in 2024, up from 14 in 2019.

s: Which programme of the Election Commission of India targets women voters, among others?
x: The ECI's SVEEP programme targets women voters.

s: In which Lok Sabha election did women's voter turnout exceed men's for the first time?
x: Women's turnout first exceeded men's in 2019 (about 67.2% vs 67.0%) and did so again in 2024.

s: In which Lok Sabha did women MPs first cross 10% of the House?
x: In the 15th Lok Sabha (2009) women MPs (59) first crossed 10%, about 10.9%.

s: What is the allocation of resources for gender-sensitive programmes called?
x: Gender budgeting allocates resources; analysis assesses impacts, planning brings gender into policy and monitoring evaluates outcomes.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ensuring survival, protection and education of the girl child
Arresting the decline in Child Sex Ratio
x: BBBP focuses on the Child Sex Ratio, preventing gender-biased sex selection and the survival, protection and education of girls; legal assistance is not its stated objective.

s: Which is the nodal Ministry for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: BBBP is a joint scheme with MWCD as nodal ministry, along with Health and Family Welfare and Education; Social Justice and Empowerment is not involved.

s: In which year was Beti Bachao Beti Padhao launched?
x: BBBP was launched in 2015, initially in 100 gender-critical districts with a low Child Sex Ratio; 'since 2006' is wrong.

s: Where was Beti Bachao Beti Padhao launched on 22 January 2015?
x: BBBP was launched at Panipat (Haryana) on 22 January 2015. Ballia and Mahoba are the launch places of Ujjwala and Ujjwala 2.0.

s: How is Beti Bachao Beti Padhao funded?
x: BBBP is 100% centrally funded, with an initial outlay of ₹100 crore.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It falls under the Samarthya vertical of Mission Shakti
Its nodal ministry is Women and Child Development
x: BBBP falls under Sambal (safety), not Samarthya (empowerment), of Mission Shakti.

s: Besides the Ministry of Women and Child Development, which Ministries jointly run Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Social Justice & Empowerment and Health & Family Welfare
x: BBBP is led by MWCD with the Ministries of Health & Family Welfare and Education; Social Justice is not involved.

s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is a flagship programme of the Prime Minister along with which of the following?
x: BBBP is one of the PM's flagship programmes along with Make in India and Digital India; Antyodaya Yojana is not one.

s: How many gender-critical districts did Beti Bachao Beti Padhao cover at its launch?
x: BBBP began in 100 gender-critical districts with low CSR and now covers all districts.

s: On what basis were the first districts chosen under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
x: BBBP first covered gender-critical districts, that is, districts with a low child sex ratio.

s: Ujjwala 2.0, launched in August 2021 at Mahoba, provided which additional features?
o: Antenatal care and maternity cash assistance
Free second LPG cylinder and permanent housing for migrants
Free first refill and hotplate, with self-declaration of address for migrant families
Interest-free loans for LPG distributors only
x: Ujjwala 2.0 provided a free first refill and hotplate. Migrant families were permitted to self-declare their address.

s: Where was Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched on 1 May 2016?
x: PMUY, under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, was launched at Ballia (UP) to give LPG connections to women of BPL households.

s: How does Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana mainly improve women's health?
o: Giving LPG connections in women's names to end indoor smoke
Giving free antenatal check-ups every month
x: Ujjwala gives LPG connections in women's names, which ends indoor smoke from wood fires and so improves their health.

s: Which Ministry implements Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana?
x: Ujjwala, launched on 1 May 2016 at Ballia, is a scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana?
o: It gives free LPG connections to BPL women
It was launched at Ballia in 2016
Ujjwala 2.0 gave a free first refill and hotplate
It is an anti-trafficking scheme of 2007
x: The 2007 anti-trafficking scheme is Ujjawala (now in Shakti Sadan); Ujjwala (2016) is the LPG scheme.

s: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana has reached over how many households (2026)?
x: PMUY has reached over 10.5 crore households (2026).

s: What did Ujjawala, the women's welfare scheme, mainly deal with?
o: Deposit-free LPG connections for poor households
Prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation
x: Ujjawala was concerned with prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation. Deposit-free LPG connections belong to PM Ujjwala Yojana, a separate scheme.

s: What is Mahila e-Haat?
o: A credit scheme exclusively for SC/ST entrepreneurs
An online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups
A maternity cash-transfer programme for pregnant women
A residential shelter for women in distress
x: Mahila e-Haat is an MWCD online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups. It was started in 2016 and is run by Rashtriya Mahila Kosh.

s: Under which Ministry is the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (1993) a registered society?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: RMK is under the Ministry of WCD and lends to NGOs/MFIs that on-lend micro-credit to poor women; Finance runs Stand-Up India.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Stand-Up India?
o: It is restricted to existing enterprises only.
It is associated with the Ministry of Finance.
It provides bank loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
Each bank branch must support at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.
x: Stand-Up India is for new (greenfield) enterprises, not existing ones.

s: DAY-NRLM is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: DAY-NRLM is a Ministry of Rural Development programme. It was launched as Aajeevika in 2011 and renamed in 2016.

s: Under DAY-NRLM, what is an SHG member who earns at least ₹1 lakh a year called?
x: Under DAY-NRLM, an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh annually is termed a Lakhpati Didi.

s: Stand-Up India is a scheme of which Ministry?
x: Stand-Up India (2016) is under the Ministry of Finance; DAY-NRLM is under Rural Development.

s: Stand-Up India gives loans of what range for greenfield enterprises?
x: Stand-Up India gives ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for new (greenfield) enterprises, not existing ones.

s: Under what name was DAY-NRLM launched in 2011?
x: DAY-NRLM began in 2011 as Aajeevika and was renamed in 2016.

s: How does the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh provide micro-credit to poor women?
o: Through NGOs and MFIs that on-lend to poor women
x: RMK (1993), a registered society under MWCD, lends to NGOs/MFIs, which on-lend micro-credit to poor women.

s: What is the interest rate on the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate?
x: The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is a 2-year deposit of ₹1,000-₹2 lakh at 7.5% interest.

s: Under Stand-Up India, each bank branch must lend to at least which borrowers?
o: One SC/ST and one woman borrower
One minority and one woman borrower
One SC and one ST borrower
x: Stand-Up India requires at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per bank branch.

s: Under Stand-Up India, what minimum holding must an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur have in a non-individual enterprise?
x: In non-individual enterprises, at least 51% holding must be with an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur.

s: Which body runs Mahila e-Haat, launched in 2016?
x: Mahila e-Haat, MWCD's 2016 online platform for women entrepreneurs, is run by the Rashtriya Mahila Kosh.

s: What is the tenure of the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate?
x: The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is a 2-year deposit of Rs 1,000 to Rs 2 lakh at 7.5%.

s: STEP, introduced during 1986–87, was designed to promote which of the following?
o: Fast-track trials of crimes against women
Skills for gainful employment of women
x: STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.

s: Which one of the following statements about DWCRA is correct?
o: It was a sub-scheme of IRDP for groups of rural women, initiated in 1982-83.
It was an urban poverty mission launched in 2007.
It was an interest subsidy programme introduced in 2004.
It was a World Bank-aided project implemented only in municipalities.
x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the Integrated Rural Development Programme for groups of rural women and began in 1982-83.

s: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 1993, seeks to promote which one of the following among rural women?
x: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 1993 to encourage the savings habit among rural women.

s: What was the purpose of Swayam Siddha (2001)?
x: Swayam Siddha (2001) was an SHG-based holistic empowerment scheme; Ujjawala dealt with trafficking and Swadhar Greh with women in difficult circumstances.

s: Girls of which age group get vocational training through PMKVY 4.0 under NAVYA (2025-26)?
x: NAVYA, an MSDE-MWCD initiative, trains girls aged 16-18 in 27 aspirational districts in 19 States.

s: What is the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015), introduced under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: A vocational training scheme for adolescent girls
A post-birth grant for girls of BPL families
A pension scheme for women above 60 years
A small-savings account for a girl below 10 years
x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 2015 under BBBP, is a small-savings account for girls below 10 years, mainly for education and marriage.

s: In which year was Dhanalakshmi, a conditional cash transfer scheme for the girl child, launched?
x: Dhanalakshmi (2008) linked cash to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and delaying marriage beyond 18.

s: Balika Samriddhi Yojana, launched in 1997, provides which of the following benefits?
o: A savings account for girls below 10 years of age
Post-birth grants and annual scholarships for girls belonging to BPL families
Nutrition and life-skills training for adolescent girls under ICDS
Conditional cash transfers for immunisation and delayed marriage
x: Balika Samriddhi Yojana provides a post-birth grant and annual scholarships to girls from families living below the poverty line.

s: What did Kishori Shakti Yojana (2000) provide to adolescent girls?
x: Kishori Shakti Yojana gave ICDS-based nutrition, health and life-skills to adolescent girls.

s: A Sukanya Samriddhi account can be opened for a girl below what age?
x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015) is a small-savings account for a girl below 10, for her education and marriage.

s:
Consider the following statements about the launch years of schemes:
1. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana was launched in 2015.
2. Balika Samriddhi Yojana was launched in 1993.
3. Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was launched in 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sukanya is 2015 and Mahila Samriddhi 1993; Balika Samriddhi Yojana was launched in 1997, not 1993.

s: NAVYA (2025-26), which trains girls under PMKVY 4.0, is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development and which Ministry?
x: NAVYA is run by MSDE and MWCD for girls aged 16-18 in 27 aspirational districts.

s: Under Mission Shakti, Shakti Sadan and PMMVY fall under which sub-scheme?
x: Samarthya is the empowerment component (Shakti Sadan, PMMVY); Sambal is the safety component (OSC, 181, Nari Adalat).

s: From 1 April 2022, which component is included under Mission Poshan 2.0?
o: One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls
Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas and PMMVY
Child Protection Services and the Juvenile Justice system
x: Mission Poshan 2.0 comprises Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.

s: What does the 'Sambal' vertical of Mission Shakti deal with?
x: Sambal concerns women's safety and Samarthya women's empowerment.

s: Of which mission is SABLA (Scheme for Adolescent Girls) now a part?
x: SABLA, covering nutrition, life-skills and health of adolescent girls, is now part of Poshan 2.0, not Samarthya.

s: Which umbrella mission of the Ministry of Women and Child Development covers child protection, foster care and juvenile justice homes?
x: Mission Vatsalya covers child protection, foster care and juvenile justice homes. LPG connections in women's names come under Ujjwala.

s: Which Ministry administers Mission Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0?
x: POSHAN 2.0, covering ages 0–6 with Poshan Tracker and Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi, comes under WCD.

s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao operates under which vertical of Mission Shakti?
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is included under the Sambal vertical, which deals with women’s safety.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Childline 1098 – Early childhood care and education
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana – Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam – Law & Justice
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi – Early childhood care and education
x: Childline 1098 is integrated with helpline 112 under Mission Vatsalya; ECCE is the focus of Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi.

s: Under Mission Vatsalya, with which number has Childline 1098 been integrated?
x: Mission Vatsalya integrates Childline 1098 with the emergency number 112.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the umbrella missions of the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
x: From 1 April 2022 MWCD schemes fall under three missions: Shakti, Vatsalya and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0; Mission Indradhanush is an immunisation drive of the Health Ministry.

s: Which earlier scheme was subsumed in Mission Vatsalya?
x: Mission Vatsalya, for child protection, subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS).

s: With which law is Mission Vatsalya aligned?
x: Mission Vatsalya runs child protection and juvenile justice homes in line with the JJ Act, 2015.

s: What does 'Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi' under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 focus on?
x: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi adds early childhood care and education (ECCE) to Anganwadi services.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Sambal sub-scheme?
x: One Stop Centre, Women Helpline 181 and Nari Adalat are components of Sambal. Palna is a component of Samarthya.

s: Shakti Sadan was formed by merging which two earlier schemes?
o: Working Women Hostel and National Creche Scheme
x: Shakti Sadan was created by merging Swadhar Greh and Ujjawala under Samarthya.

s: One Stop Centre (Sakhi) provides which services under one roof?
o: Medical, legal, counselling and shelter support
x: One Stop Centre provides medical, legal, counselling and shelter support under one roof and is funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.

s: What is the main purpose of Nari Adalat under Mission Shakti?
o: Alternative grievance redressal in petty cases such as harassment and denial of entitlements
Selection of beneficiaries for LPG connections
Distribution of maternity benefits to government employees
Trial of serious criminal offences by regular courts
x: Nari Adalat provides an alternative grievance-redressal mechanism for petty cases, including harassment and denial of entitlements.

s: What does 'Palna' provide under Mission Shakti?
x: Palna runs crèches; Sakhi Niwas runs working-women hostels and PMMVY gives maternity benefit.

s: With which institution did the Ministry of Women and Child Development launch Stree Mano Raksha for women's mental health in March 2022?
x: Stree Mano Raksha is an MWCD project with NIMHANS, Bengaluru for the mental health of women (APPSC 2021 key). AIIMS and ICMR are not the partners, and NLSIU is the partner in Nirbhay Raho, not this project.

s: Which of the following initiatives has been discontinued?
o: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers
One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
x: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers have been discontinued. The other options refer to continuing schemes or sub-schemes.

s: From which fund is the One Stop Centre (Sakhi) under Mission Shakti funded?
x: One Stop Centres and Women Helpline 181 under Sambal are funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.

s: What is the number of the Women Helpline under the Sambal sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?
x: Women Helpline 181 runs 24x7 and is being integrated with ERSS-112; 1098 is Childline.

s: What does Sakhi Niwas under the Samarthya sub-scheme of Mission Shakti provide?
o: One-stop help for women facing violence
x: Sakhi Niwas is the new name of the Working Women Hostel scheme; Palna gives creches and Shakti Sadan gives shelter.

s: What is SANKALP-HEW under the Samarthya sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?
o: A health insurance scheme for women
A hub for the empowerment of women
x: SANKALP-HEW is a Hub for Empowerment of Women under Samarthya.

s: Swadhar Greh is intended primarily for which target group?
x: Swadhar Greh is meant for women in difficult circumstances and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.

s: On which day does the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan provide free antenatal check-ups?
o: The first day of every month
The fifteenth day of every month
The fifth day of every month
The ninth day of every month
x: PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on the ninth day of every month.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IGMSY – Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month
PMMVY – Partial wage-loss compensation for the first living child
PMSMA – Institutional-delivery cash assistance under NHM
x: PMMVY gives partial wage-loss compensation; IGMSY was the pilot maternity benefit, PMSMA gives ninth-of-month antenatal check-ups and JSY supports institutional delivery.

s: Which statement correctly describes PMMVY 2.0?
o: It provides ₹5,000 for the first child and ₹6,000 for a second child if the second child is a girl.
It provides ₹5,000 only to regular government employees.
It was introduced from 2016 under Mission Vatsalya.
It provides ₹6,000 for every second child irrespective of sex.
x: PMMVY 2.0, implemented from 2022 under Mission Shakti, provides ₹5,000 for the first child and ₹6,000 for a second child if the second child is a girl. Regular government employees are excluded.

s: Before PMMVY 2.0, the ₹5,000 PMMVY benefit was paid in how many instalments?
x: The ₹5,000 was earlier paid in three instalments: ₹1,000 + ₹2,000 + ₹2,000.

s: Which group is excluded from PMMVY 2.0?
o: Mothers of a second girl child
x: PMMVY 2.0 excludes regular government employees; it gives ₹5,000 for the first child and ₹6,000 for a second child if a girl.

s: Which 2010 pilot maternity benefit scheme was the forerunner of PMMVY?
x: IGMSY (2010) was the pilot maternity benefit scheme that preceded PMMVY.

s: For what does Janani Suraksha Yojana (2005) give cash?
x: JSY (2005), under the NHM and fully centrally funded, gives cash for institutional delivery.

s: From which date was the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) implemented?
x: PMMVY was announced on 31 December 2016 and implemented from 1 January 2017.

s: The benefit under the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is in line with which Act?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
x: PMMVY's maternity benefit is given in line with the National Food Security Act, 2013.

s: India's Maternal Mortality Ratio has fallen from 130 to what level per lakh live births?
x: India's MMR fell from 130 to 88 per lakh live births.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Disha Bill is correct?
o: It received Presidential assent and came into force in 2019.
It was enacted by Parliament and amended only the CrPC.
It was withdrawn after receiving Presidential assent.
x: The Disha Bill never received Presidential assent; the IPC and CrPC it sought to amend were replaced by the BNS and BNSS from 1 July 2024.

s: Talliki Vandanam, the restructured form of Amma Vodi, gives eligible mothers how much a year?
x: Talliki Vandanam gives ₹15,000 a year to eligible mothers, subject to 75 per cent attendance; ₹18,750 is YSR Cheyutha.

s: What does Stree Shakti, the Andhra Pradesh scheme launched on 15 August 2025, provide?
o: Free APSRTC bus travel for women
x: Stree Shakti gives free APSRTC bus travel to girls, women and transgender persons with AP domicile.

s: YSR Cheyutha gives ₹18,750 a year to BC/SC/ST/minority women of which age group?
x: YSR Cheyutha (2020) gives ₹18,750 a year to BC/SC/ST/minority women aged 45-60.

s: Which of the following pairs of Andhra Pradesh schemes is correctly matched?
o: YSR Aasara – Free bus travel for women
Stree Shakti – ₹15,000 a year to mothers
YSR Cheyutha – Reimbursement of SHG loans
YSR Kalyanamasthu – Marriage aid for poor brides
x: Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa gives marriage aid; Aasara reimburses SHG loans, Stree Shakti gives free bus travel, and ₹15,000 to mothers is Talliki Vandanam.

s: YSR Aasara reimburses SHG loans outstanding on which date?
x: YSR Aasara reimburses SHG loans outstanding on 11 April 2019, in four instalments.

s: How many Shakti Sadans function in Andhra Pradesh as per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26?
x: AP has 26 Shakti Sadans sheltering 950 women (AP SES 2025-26).

s: What does Article 244A of the Constitution provide for?
o: Reservation in posts for backward classes
x: Article 244A, inserted by the 22nd Amendment in 1969, provides for an Autonomous State within Assam; 244(1) and 244(2) cover the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject
o: Article 46 — Educational and economic interests of SCs and STs
Article 342 — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
x: Article 46 concerns the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs. Article 342 concerns notification of STs, Article 338A establishes the NCST, and Article 275(1) concerns grants-in-aid.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 15(5) permits admission quotas in minority educational institutions.
Article 15(4) provides special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs.
Article 16(4) concerns reservation of posts for inadequately represented backward classes.
x: Article 15(5) excludes minority educational institutions from its scope.

s: Which Article provides for reservation of seats for SCs and STs in State Legislative Assemblies?
x: Article 332 covers State Assemblies and Article 330 the Lok Sabha; there is no SC/ST reservation in the Rajya Sabha.

s: Under which provision are Scheduled Areas declared?
x: Scheduled Areas are declared under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule; Article 339 provides for Union control and a Commission on their administration.

s: Which Article requires SC/ST claims in services to be considered consistently with the efficiency of administration?
x: Article 335 requires SC/ST claims to posts to be considered consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration.

s: Which of the following constitutional provisions deals with reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in local bodies?
x: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Articles with the lists they deal with?
x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the Scheduled Tribes and Article 342A the socially and educationally backward classes.

s: Which reservation clause was added to the Constitution by the First Amendment, 1951?
x: Article 15(4) was the first reservation clause added by amendment (First Amendment, 1951); Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution.

s: Under which Article is the list of Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory specified?
x: Article 342 deals with the specification of Scheduled Tribes; ST status is not restricted by religion.

s: Which States replaced Bihar in the proviso to Article 164(1) through the 94th Amendment (2006)?
x: The 94th Amendment replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand in the list of States needing a Tribal Welfare Minister.

s:
Consider the following statements about the proviso to Article 164(1):
1. The Tribal Welfare Minister may also hold charge of SC and BC welfare.
2. Odisha and Madhya Pradesh are among the States covered.
3. The 94th Amendment added Bihar to the list.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the 94th Amendment (2006) removed Bihar, replacing it with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

s: Which Directive Principle Article directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs?
x: Article 46 (DPSP) covers the educational and economic interests of SCs/STs and their protection from social injustice.

s: Which Article provides for Union control over the administration of Scheduled Areas?
x: Article 339 deals with Union control of Scheduled Areas and the Commission on Scheduled Areas.

s: Under the proviso to Article 164(1), which State is NOT required to have a Minister for Tribal Welfare?
x: The proviso covers Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; the 94th Amendment (2006) removed Bihar.

s: Which Article provides grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 275(1) provides grants-in-aid from the CFI for ST welfare; Article 339 gives the Union control of Scheduled Areas.

s: In which Part of the Constitution are Articles 330 to 342, the special provisions relating to certain classes, placed?
x: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) contains special provisions for SCs, STs and other classes; Part XV is Elections and Part XVII is Official Language.

s: To which States does the Sixth Schedule under Article 244(2) apply?
o: Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Mizoram
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh
x: Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule cover tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; other Scheduled Areas fall under the Fifth Schedule.

s: Which clause of Article 366 defines 'Scheduled Castes'?
x: Article 366(24) defines Scheduled Castes and 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes.

s: Under which clause of Article 366 are 'Scheduled Tribes' defined?
x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes; 366(24) defines Scheduled Castes.

s: Article 334 originally prescribed the reservation of seats for SCs and STs for how many years?
x: Article 334 originally fixed a 10-year limit, later extended by amendments; it now runs to 2030, not 2035.

s: Which is the ST-reserved Lok Sabha constituency of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Araku is AP's only ST Lok Sabha seat; of 25 seats, 4 are SC and 1 is ST.

s: On the basis of which Census figures and through which Amendments were SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha refixed?
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.

s: For which States did the 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984 provide ST seats in the Lok Sabha?
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.

s: To what number did the 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill (April 2026) seek to raise the strength of the Lok Sabha?
x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850; it was not passed.

s: Which Amendment most recently extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334, up to 2030?
x: The extensions came through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended reservation to 2030.

s: Who elects the representative of a constituency reserved for SCs or STs in a legislature?
o: Only SC/ST voters of the constituency
An electoral college of local bodies
x: Reserved seats are proportionate to population, but there are no separate electorates; all voters in the constituency elect the representative.

s: How many of Andhra Pradesh's 175 Assembly seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: The AP Assembly has 29 SC and 7 ST seats out of 175.

s: How many of Andhra Pradesh's 25 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: AP has 4 SC seats and 1 ST seat (Araku) among its 25 Lok Sabha seats.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reserved seats for SCs and STs?
o: Seats are reserved in proportion to population
Seats are reserved in the Rajya Sabha too
x: Articles 330 and 332 reserve seats only in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; there are no SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha.

s: Besides extending SC/ST seat reservation to 2030, what did the 104th Amendment (2019) do?
x: The 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination; women's reservation (334A) is the 106th.

s: Which Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation in legislatures up to 2020?
x: The 95th Amendment (2009) extended the reservation to 2020; the 104th took it to 2030.

s: After the 2008 delimitation, how many Lok Sabha seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes respectively?
x: Reserved Lok Sabha seats rose from 79 SC / 41 ST (1971 Census) to 84 SC / 47 ST after the 2008 delimitation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a form of untouchability?
o: The two-tumbler system in tea shops
x: Temple-entry denial, residential segregation and the two-tumbler system are forms of untouchability; reservation of seats is a protective measure, not such a practice.

s: In the context of untouchability, what does "structural violence" mean?
x: Structural violence, a concept associated with Johan Galtung, is harm built into social structures.

s: In the Sabarimala reference, in what manner did Justice B.V. Nagarathna say Article 17 cannot be applied?
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.

s: Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) belongs to which group of Fundamental Rights?
x: Article 17 is in the Right to Equality group and operates against private persons too; the Constitution does not define 'untouchability'.

s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.

s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution, who has the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17?
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.

s: How did the Mysore High Court interpret 'untouchability' under Article 17?
o: The practice as defined in the 1955 Act
Including social boycott of a few individuals
The practice as it developed historically
x: The Mysore HC read it as the historically developed practice, which excludes social boycott of a few individuals.

s: Why is the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 significant?
o: The first law providing reservation in the Lok Sabha
The first law using the expression Scheduled Tribes
The first law creating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enacted to enforce Article 17. The Government of India Act, 1935 had earlier used the term Scheduled Castes.

s: Under what name was the first post-1950 list of Scheduled Castes issued?
x: The first list after 1950 was the Constitution (SC) Order, 1950; the first list was of 1936 under the GoI Act 1935.

s: Where is 'untouchability' defined?
o: It is not defined in the Constitution or any Act
x: Untouchability is not defined in the Constitution or any Act; the Mysore HC read it as the practice as historically developed.

s: Which case held that Article 17 binds private persons too?
x: Article 17 applies horizontally to private persons, as held in PUDR v. Union of India (1982).

s: Who first used the term 'Scheduled Castes'?
x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission and given shape in the Government of India Act, 1935.

s: In which year was the first list of Scheduled Castes issued under the Government of India Act, 1935?
x: The term took shape in the GoI Act 1935 and the first list came in 1936; the first post-1950 list was the Constitution (SC) Order, 1950.

s: Who gave the concept of 'structural violence', used to describe untouchability?
x: Johan Galtung described structural violence as harm built into social structures.

s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.

s: How has manual scavenging been described?
o: Oldest surviving form of bonded labour
Worst surviving form of child labour
Last surviving form of forced labour
x: Manual scavenging is described as the “worst surviving symbol of untouchability.”

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013?
o: It prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.
It provides for rehabilitation of manual scavengers with alternative livelihoods.
It permits hazardous manual cleaning when done by private contractors.
x: The 2013 Act bans hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by anyone, including private contractors, and requires mechanisation and rehabilitation.

s: Which group does NSKFDC support among economic empowerment measures for disadvantaged communities?
x: NSKFDC supports sanitation workers; NSFDC covers SCs below the poverty line, PM-DAKSH skill development and VCF-SC economic support for SCs.

s: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013?
o: Identification and rehabilitation of affected persons
Prohibition of cleaning sewers and septic tanks without protective gear
Legalisation of dry latrines under regulated conditions
x: The 2013 Act does not legalise dry latrines.

s: NAMASTE is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and which other Ministry?
x: NAMASTE, aimed at zero sanitation deaths, is run jointly by MoSJE and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

s: When did the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 come into force?
x: The 2013 Act came into force on 6 December 2013.

s: As of August 2026, about how many manual scavengers had been identified in India?
x: About 58,000 manual scavengers were identified; 90,915 is the sewer/septic workers profiled and 2,652 the projects approved.

s: Which Kerala start-up developed Bandicoot, the manhole-cleaning robot meant to replace manual scavenging?
x: Bandicoot was developed by the Kerala start-up Genrobotics to clean manholes without manual scavenging.

s: Which corporation gives economic support to Scheduled Castes living below the poverty line?
x: NSFDC funds BPL Scheduled Castes; NSKFDC is for sanitation workers.

s: PM-DAKSH, one of the economic measures for disadvantaged communities, is mainly about what?
x: PM-DAKSH is for skills; VCF-SC gives venture capital and NSFDC supports BPL SCs.

s: The Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) has been subsumed in which scheme?
x: SRMS (2007, revised 2013 and 2021) has been subsumed in NAMASTE, which aims at zero sanitation deaths.

s: With which movement is Bezwada Wilson, winner of the 2016 Ramon Magsaysay Award, associated?
x: Bezwada Wilson is a founder of the Safai Karmachari Andolan against manual scavenging.

s: Which legislation prohibited the employment of manual scavengers and the construction of dry latrines?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
x: The 1993 Act prohibited employing manual scavengers and constructing dry latrines. The 2013 Act subsequently widened the prohibition and rehabilitation framework.

s: The National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation was established in which year and serves as the nodal agency for which scheme?
o: 1997 — Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers
x: NSKFDC was established in 1997 and is the nodal agency for the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers.

s: Which body monitors the implementation of measures relating to manual scavenging and rehabilitation?
x: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitors implementation in this field.

s: To how much was the compensation for each sewer death raised in Balram Singh (2023)?
x: Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) ordered ₹10 lakh; Balram Singh (2023) raised it to ₹30 lakh.

s: NAMASTE, launched in 2023, is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Replacing all State Vigilance and Monitoring Committees
Formalising sewer and septic-tank workers and achieving zero sanitation fatalities
Constructing only dry latrines in rural areas
Providing compensation exclusively for denial of public-space access
x: NAMASTE formalises sewer and septic-tank workers, subsumed the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers, and aims at zero sanitation fatalities.

s: What is the nature of offences under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013?
o: Civil wrongs punishable only with fine
Compoundable and triable only by the NCSK
x: Offences under the 2013 Act are cognizable and non-bailable; a first contravention attracts up to 1 year or Rs 50,000, and hazardous sewer cleaning up to 2 years or Rs 2 lakh. They are not non-cognizable or bailable, not mere civil wrongs, and the NCSK monitors the Act; it does not try offences.

s: What is the penalty for a first breach under the 2013 Manual Scavengers Act?
x: A first breach attracts 1 year / ₹50,000; hazardous sewer cleaning 2 years / ₹2 lakh.

s: In Safai Karamchari Andolan v Union of India (2014), what compensation did the Supreme Court fix for each sewer death since 1993?
x: The 2014 judgment fixed ₹10 lakh per sewer death since 1993; Balram Singh (2023) raised it to ₹30 lakh.

s: Under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, what is the penalty for a first breach involving hazardous sewer cleaning?
x: Hazardous sewer cleaning carries 2 years and/or Rs 2 lakh for a first breach; other first breaches carry 1 year and/or Rs 50,000.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the list of Scheduled Castes of a State?
o: The President notifies it after consulting the Governor.
The State Legislature notifies it by resolution.
The Governor notifies it with the State Legislature's approval.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes notifies it by order.
x: Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes of a State after consulting the Governor; later inclusion or exclusion can be made only by Parliament by law.

s: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, what did the Supreme Court hold about a Scheduled Caste person who converts to Christianity?
o: Cannot claim SC status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity
Can claim SC status on the State Government's recommendation alone
Retains SC status because religion is irrelevant to the SC list
x: A Christian convert cannot claim SC status merely on earlier caste identity; reconversion requires proof of original SC status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community.

s: As per Census 2011, how many caste groups are notified as Scheduled Castes?
x: 1,241 caste groups were notified as Scheduled Castes as per Census 2011.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Christian convert cannot claim Scheduled Caste status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity.
2. Scheduled Tribe status depends on the religion the person professes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Chinthada Anand (2026) denied SC status to a Christian convert, but ST status under Article 342 is religion-neutral.

s: As per Census 2011, Scheduled Castes form what share of Andhra Pradesh's population?
x: AP's SC population was 84.69 lakh, or 17.08%; 16.6% is the all-India share and 64.47% is SC literacy.

s: As per Census 2011, Scheduled Castes form what share of India's population?
x: SCs in India number 20.14 crore, or 16.6%; 17.08% is AP's share.

s: Which State has the highest share of Scheduled Castes in its population (Census 2011)?
x: Punjab has the highest SC share of population.

s: As per Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes form what share of India's population?
x: STs were 8.6% in 2011 (8.2% in 2001); SCs were 16.6%.

s: What was the literacy rate of Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh as per Census 2011?
x: SC literacy in AP was 64.47%; SCs were 17.08% of AP's population.

s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.

s: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission led directly to which scheme?
x: The Idate Commission surveyed denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes and led to the SEED scheme for their economic empowerment.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission – SC status for certain converted Dalits
Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission – Socio-economic status of Muslims
Rajiv Gauba Committee – Survey of DNTs, NTs and SNTs
Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee – Most backward SC sub-castes
x: The Balakrishnan Commission examined SC status for converted Dalits; Idate surveyed DNTs, NTs and SNTs, Gauba the most backward SC sub-castes and Sachar the Muslim community.

s: Who founded the Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS) in 1994?
x: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS in 1994, at Eedumudi in Prakasam district, not Karamchedu.

s: What was the principal demand of the Madiga Dandora movement?
o: Categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups
x: Madiga Dandora demanded categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups, or reservation within reservation.

s: The Madiga Dandora movement alleged that which community dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota?
x: The movement alleged that the Mala community disproportionately dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota, leading to the demand for a separate share.

s: The Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission placed the Malas in which category of Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Castes?
x: The Commission grouped SCs into four: A (Relli and others), B (Madiga), C (Mala) and D (Adi-Andhra).

s: Which State was the first to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by legislation, after the Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission process?
x: Andhra Pradesh became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute, through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 (Punjab had done so earlier, in 1975, only by an executive circular).

s: Which State became the first to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after the Davinder Singh judgment?
x: Telangana became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajiv Gauba Committee?
o: It concerned SC sub-castes such as the Madigas.
It was a Cabinet Secretary panel constituted in 2024.
It examined equitable mechanisms for the most backward SC sub-castes.
It was set up by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to examine ST status for the Madigas.
x: The Gauba panel was a 2024 Cabinet Secretary panel on the most backward SC sub-castes such as the Madigas; it was not a Tribal Affairs body and did not examine ST status.

s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.

s: Under which Article did the 89th Amendment (2003) create the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: The 89th Amendment split the joint commission into the NCSC (Article 338) and NCST (Article 338A); the Commissions report to the President.

s: What did the original form of Article 338 provide for?
o: a non-statutory multi-member commission appointed by the State Governments
a Special Officer designated as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
a Parliamentary committee for monitoring reservations
a separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.

s: The Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes holds which rank?
x: The NCST Chairperson has Cabinet rank, the Vice-Chairperson Minister of State rank, and members Secretary rank.

s: Besides the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, how many members does the National Commission for Scheduled Castes have?
x: Each Commission has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and 3 members; the President fixes their tenure.

s: From which date did the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes come into being?
x: After the 89th Amendment (2003) split the joint commission, the NCST came into being on 19 February 2004.

s: In which year did the joint commission for SCs and STs become a constitutional body?
x: A non-statutory Commission came in 1978; it became a constitutional joint commission in 1990 and was split in 2003.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes set up by amending Act 9 of 2003?
x: The AP State Commission for SCs and STs was set up in 2016 by amending Act 9 of 2003.

s: Who is the chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
x: K.S. Jawahar heads the AP State Commission for SCs and STs.

s: To whom does the National Commission for Scheduled Castes present its reports?
x: The NCSC has civil-court powers and reports to the President.

s: Which Amendment introduced Article 16(4B), on carrying forward unfilled reserved vacancies as a separate class?
x: The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B); such vacancies are not counted against that year's 50% ceiling.

s: Article 16(4A), permitting reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the 77th Amendment (1995) mainly in response to which judicial position?
o: Indra Sawhney (1992) confining reservation under Article 16(4) to initial appointment
E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) treating SCs as a homogeneous class
x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A). M. Nagaraj came later and upheld the 77th; Chinnaiah concerns SC sub-classification; Janhit Abhiyan concerns EWS.

s: The proviso to Article 335 relating to relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion was enabled by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.

s: With which of the following is the 85th Constitutional Amendment associated?
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.

s: Which case struck down the AP Scheduled Caste (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
x: E.V. Chinnaiah treated SCs as a single class and held that sub-classification interfered with the Article 341 list.

s: By what majority did the seven-judge Bench in State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) permit sub-classification within Scheduled Castes?
x: The Bench permitted sub-classification by 6:1, overruling E.V. Chinnaiah.

s: Which case upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Constitutional Amendments, subject to the State showing quantifiable data on specified conditions?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
x: M. Nagaraj upheld the four constitutional amendments but required quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.

s: In August 2026, what was the Centre's position on an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST reservations?
o: It left the decision to State SC Commissions
It said creamy-layer rules already apply to all SC/ST quotas
It opposed it, saying any change needs a holistic empirical review
x: The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and said any change needs a holistic empirical review.

s: Which case held that no data on backwardness is needed for SC/ST reservation in promotion and that the creamy layer applies?
x: Jarnail Singh (2018) dropped the need for backwardness data for SC/ST promotion and applied the creamy layer.

s: Which case limited Article 16(4) to initial appointment and set a 50% ceiling on reservation?
x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that 16(4) applies only at initial appointment and fixed the 50% ceiling.

s: In which year did the Karamchedu incident take place?
x: Karamchedu was in 1985, after the Siddhantam temple entry (1933) and before Tsundur (1991).

s: In 2017, for what did the NCRB add a separate crime head for SCs?
o: Being forced to leave residence or facing social boycott
Denial of reservation in educational institutions
x: The 2017 NCRB crime head covered persons forced to leave their residence or facing social boycott. Uttar Pradesh recorded 57 cases under this head that year.

s: Which body's reports list land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness and non-payment of wages as causes of caste atrocities?
o: National Commission for SCs and STs
x: Reports of the National Commission for SCs and STs list these causes; religious causes are not included.

s: Caste hierarchy, upper-caste dominance, rising Dalit activism and political interference are factors behind which of the following?
x: All four are identified as factors contributing to caste atrocities.

s: Karamchedu, Tsundur and Khairlanji are respectively associated with which States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra
Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
x: Karamchedu and Tsundur occurred in Andhra Pradesh, while Khairlanji occurred in Maharashtra.

s: Karamchedu incident is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: It resulted in monitoring by the Allahabad High Court.
It involved four members of a Dalit family in Bhandara district.
It led to the creation of the NCRB crime head for social boycott.
It sparked the independent Dalit movement.
x: The Karamchedu incident of 1985, in which Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords, sparked the independent Dalit movement.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Poona Pact
B. Ambedkar’s declaration at Yeola
C. Karamchedu incident
D. Tsundur incident
x: The Poona Pact took place in 1932, the Yeola declaration in 1935, Karamchedu in 1985 and Tsundur in 1991.

s: In the Hathras case, to whom did the Supreme Court entrust monitoring?
x: In the Hathras case, the Supreme Court entrusted monitoring to the Allahabad High Court.

s: As per NCRB data for 2023, which State recorded the most crimes against Scheduled Castes?
x: Uttar Pradesh (15,130) led, followed by Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, out of 57,789 cases.

s: Where did B.R. Ambedkar declare "I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu"?
x: B. R. Ambedkar made this declaration at Yeola in 1935.

s: In which period was the Adi-Andhra movement, which claimed Dalits were the original inhabitants of Andhra, mainly active?
x: The movement was active in the 1910s–30s and demanded access to education, temples and tanks.

s: Who criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic?
x: Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic; Gandhi used the term 'Harijan'.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Jagan Mitra Mandali — Bhagya Reddy Varma
Harijan Sevak Sangh — Manda Krishna Madiga
x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was associated with Gandhi, whereas Manda Krishna Madiga led the Madiga Dandora movement.

s:
Assertion (A): Ambedkar advocated legal-constitutional rights and the annihilation of caste.
Reason (R): Ambedkar supported reform of caste only from within Hindu society.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is correct; R is false because reform from within is associated with Gandhi, not Ambedkar.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Andhra Dalit newspapers is correct?
x: Adi Andhra was associated with Didla Pullaiah, while Nava Jeevan was associated with Undru Subbarao.

s: What is the central idea of Gurram Jashuva's Gabbilam?
o: A bat can enter a temple while an untouchable cannot
A king grants land to temple servants
A crow carries a message from Buddha to an emperor
A temple priest abolishes caste through ritual
x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.

s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Vaikom Satyagraha is correct?
o: Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924–25
x: Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore in 1924–25 and was organised by T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon, with K. Kelappan also associated with it.

s: Which right of Dalits did B.R. Ambedkar assert through the Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha?
o: Draw water from a public tank
Use roads around the Vaikom temple
x: The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
