s: When was the Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha led by B.R. Ambedkar held?
x: The Mahad Satyagraha was on 20 March 1927 (centenary from 20 March 2026); the Manusmriti Dahan was on 25 December 1927.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: The Siddhantam Temple Entry movement took place in Krishna district in 1933 and was one of the earliest such movements in Andhra. The other options confuse its details with those of other movements.

s: Which of the following pairs (Work – Author) is correctly matched?
x: Jatimimamsa is by Sree Narayana Guru; Gabbilam is by Gurram Jashuva, Annihilation of Caste by B.R. Ambedkar and Gulamgiri by Jyotiba Phule.

s: What was the name of the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State, set up by Bhagya Reddy Varma?
x: Bhagya Reddy Varma established Jagan Mitra Mandali in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.

s: Who founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932?
x: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932 after the Poona Pact; Bhagya Reddy Varma called it paternalistic.

s: Where did the Kalaram Temple Entry Satyagraha (1930) led by Ambedkar take place?
x: The Kalaram Temple Entry Satyagraha was at Nashik in 1930; Mahad (1927) was about water from a public tank.

s: Who is the author of Gulamgiri (1873)?
x: Gulamgiri (slavery) is by Jyotiba Phule; Annihilation of Caste is Ambedkar's and Gabbilam is Jashuva's.

s: Who held that political freedom is meaningless without social equality?
x: Periyar stressed self-respect and held political freedom meaningless without social equality.

s: Which of the following pairs (Leader – Statement or idea) is correctly matched?
o: Ambedkar – Untouchability is a blot on Hinduism
Periyar – I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu
Gandhi – Caste is a division of labourers
x: Gandhi coined 'Harijan' and called untouchability a blot on Hinduism; the Yeola declaration and 'division of labourers' are Ambedkar's.

s: On which date did B.R. Ambedkar burn the Manusmriti (Manusmriti Dahan)?
x: Ambedkar burnt the Manusmriti on 25 December 1927, after the Mahad Satyagraha of 20 March 1927.

s: In which year did Gandhi start the paper 'Harijan'?
x: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932 and started the paper Harijan in 1933.

s: Who is the author of 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936)?
x: Annihilation of Caste (1936) was written by B.R. Ambedkar.

s: Which of the following law–purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act – Prevents atrocities against SCs/STs
Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 – Eliminates manual scavenging
Protection of Civil Rights Act – Establishes NHRC
Protection of Human Rights Act – Establishes NHRC
x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act punishes the practice of untouchability; the NHRC was set up by the Protection of Human Rights Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Civil Rights Act?
o: It prescribes penalties for practising untouchability.
It was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability (Offences) Act.
It came into force on 1 June 1955.
It came into force on 30 January 1990.
x: The Act came into force on 1 June 1955; 30 January 1990 is the commencement date of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

s: Under which provision does a conviction for an untouchability offence lead to disqualification from contesting elections?
o: Section 7 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.

s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 primarily prescribes penalties for which of the following?
o: Denying forest rights to traditional forest dwellers
Enforcing religious and social disabilities arising from untouchability
x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, punishes enforcing religious and social disabilities that come from untouchability. Child labour and sex determination fall under other Acts.

s: From which Article does the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 mainly derive its constitutional basis?
x: The Act was enacted to give effect to Article 17 of the Constitution, which abolishes untouchability.

s: What was the original name of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
x: It was enacted under Article 17 as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 and renamed in 1976; it extends to the whole of India.

s: Which of the following is correct about the expression 'untouchability'?
o: It is expressly defined in the Constitution.
It is expressly defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
The Mysore High Court interpreted it as a historically developed caste practice.
It is defined in both the Constitution and the 1955 Act.
x: The term is defined in neither the Constitution nor the Act; the Mysore High Court read it as the historically developed practice.

s: In which year was the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act?
x: The Act was renamed in 1976; the PCR Rules came in 1977.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955:
1. It extends to the whole of India.
2. Its Rules were framed in 1995.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The PCR Act extends to the whole of India (s.1(2)); its Rules were framed in 1977, while 1995 is the year of the PoA Rules.

s: What is the nature of offences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Non-cognizable and triable only by a Sessions Court
Cognizable only with prior sanction of the State Government
x: Under Section 15, offences under the PCR Act are cognizable and may be tried summarily; they are also non-compoundable (MPPSC 2019 accepted both descriptions). They are not non-cognizable or compoundable, are not reserved for Sessions Courts, and need no prior sanction.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Section 3 — Religious disabilities relating to entry into public places of worship
Section 6 — Collective fine on inhabitants of an area
Section 15A — Refusal to sell goods or render services
x: Section 3 deals with religious disabilities, including barring entry to or worship in public places of worship. Section 6 concerns refusal to sell goods or render services, Section 10A concerns collective fines and Section 15A concerns State duties.

s: What does Section 10A of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 provide for?
x: Section 10A provides for a collective fine; Section 5 covers refusal of admission and Section 12 the presumption.

s: What is the punishment for a first offence under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Imprisonment from one to six months and fine from ₹100 to ₹500
Imprisonment up to three years without fine
Imprisonment from six months to one year and fine from ₹500 to ₹1,000
x: For a first offence, the stated punishment is imprisonment of one to six months and a fine of ₹100 to ₹500. The older wording is also expressed as imprisonment up to six months or fine up to ₹500 or both.

s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry at the Union level for the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal ministry, with the Ministry of Home Affairs also associated with implementation.

s: In Sukanya Shantha (2024), what did the Supreme Court hold that Article 17 bars?
o: Only physical exclusion from public wells and temples
Only untouchability imposed by private employers
Only untouchability not followed by customary communities
x: Sukanya Shantha held that Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma, reading untouchability beyond physical exclusion.

s: A person convicted under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is also subject to which electoral consequence mentioned in the law?
o: Permanent disqualification from voting in all elections
Disqualification from holding any private office
Disqualification from contesting elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
x: A person convicted under the Act is disqualified from contesting elections to Parliament or a State Legislature.

s: In which year were the Protection of Civil Rights Rules framed?
x: The PCR Rules date from 1977; the PoA Rules from 1995.

s: Under which Section of the Protection of Civil Rights Act is preaching or justifying untouchability punishable?
x: Section 7 covers insulting an SC member and preaching or justifying untouchability.

s: What does Section 15A of the Protection of Civil Rights Act deal with?
x: Section 15A lists State duties: legal aid, special courts, surveys of prone areas, vigilance officers and annual reports.

s: Under which Section of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is refusing to sell goods or render services on the ground of untouchability punishable?
x: PCR Section 6 punishes refusal to sell goods or render services; Section 5 covers hospitals and schools.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is correctly matched?
x: The Act was passed in 1989 and came into force on 30 January 1990; it was amended on 20 August 2018, adding Section 18A.

s: Since when has the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act applied to Jammu and Kashmir?
x: The PoA Act applies to J&K since 2019.

s: Which law was enacted because the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 proved inadequate to check atrocities against SCs and STs?
o: Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013
x: The PCR Act could not check atrocities against SCs/STs, so Parliament enacted the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in 1989.

s: On which date did the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 receive the President's assent?
x: The PoA Act got assent on 11 September 1989 and came into force on 30 January 1990.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: It creates offences not covered by the PCR Act or the IPC.
Section 3 deals with atrocities by persons who are not SC/ST members.
It applies only when the accused and victim belong to the same SC or ST.
Section 18 bars anticipatory bail for the accused.
x: The Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.

s: By whom are the offences covered by the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act mainly committed?
o: Members of the same Scheduled Caste
x: The Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.

s: Which of the following is NOT a provision associated with the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Grant of arms licences to members of SCs and STs
Enhanced punishment for public servants in specified circumstances
Cancellation of arms licences in atrocity-prone areas
Automatic dissolution of every local authority located in an atrocity-prone area
x: The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants. It does not provide for automatic dissolution of local authorities.

s: Within how many days does an appeal from an order of a Special Court under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, including a bail order, lie to the High Court?
x: An appeal, including an appeal against a bail order, lies to the High Court within 90 days.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched under the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Section 4 – Wilful neglect of duty by public servants
Section 19 – Appeal to the High Court within 90 days
Section 14A – Appeal to the High Court within 90 days
Section 23 – Rule-making power of the Central Government
x: Section 19 bars probation for convicts; the 90-day appeal to the High Court is Section 14A.

s: Which Section of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act provides for Special Public Prosecutors?
x: Section 15 provides Special Public Prosecutors; Section 14 provides Special Courts.

s: Which Section of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act bars the release of a convict on probation?
x: Section 19 bars probation; Section 18 bars anticipatory bail, 18A removes preliminary enquiry and Section 23 gives rule-making power.

s: Under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, the State Government specifies a Court of Session as a Special Court with the concurrence of whom?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: A Special Court is a Court of Session specified by the State Government with the concurrence of the High Court Chief Justice.

s: Under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Rules, within how many days must police investigation ordinarily be completed?
x: The investigation is to be completed within 60 days; the Act dates from 1989 and the Rules from 1995.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the machinery for prevention of atrocities?
o: The State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Chief Minister.
SC/ST Protection Cells function under an IG or ADGP of Police.
A Secretary-level nodal officer is designated in each State.
The District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Superintendent of Police.
x: The District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Collector.

s: What is the number of the National Toll-Free Helpline against casteism and atrocities?
x: 14566 is the national helpline against caste atrocities. 1098 is Childline, 181 the women's helpline, and 1930 the cyber-crime helpline.

s: Who heads the State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee under the PoA Rules, 1995?
x: The State committee is headed by the Chief Minister; the District committee by the Collector.

s: Who heads the District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee under Rule 17 of the PoA Rules, 1995?
x: Rule 17 sets up a District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee in each district, headed by the Collector/DM.

s: What is the range of relief to atrocity victims under the PoA Rules (2016)?
x: Since 2016 relief ranges from ₹85,000 to ₹8.25 lakh.

s:
Consider the following statements about investigation under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995:
1. It is done by an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
2. The charge-sheet is to be filed within 60 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Under the PoA Rules, 1995, an officer not below DSP investigates and the charge-sheet must be filed within 60 days.

s: Under the 2015 amendment, within what time is the trial in an Exclusive Special Court to be completed?
o: 60 days of filing of the charge-sheet
90 days of arrest of the accused
30 days of registration of the FIR
x: The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.

s: On what did the 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act add a new chapter?
x: The 2015 amendment introduced a new chapter on the rights of victims and witnesses.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the 2015 amendment to the Atrocities Act is correctly matched?
o: Exclusive Special Public Prosecutors – Part of the original 1989 Act
Special Court cognizance – Needs prior Central approval
Exclusive Special Courts – Inserted by the 2015 amendment
Direct cognizance by Special Courts – Barred
x: The 2015 amendment added Exclusive Special Courts and Exclusive Special PPs and let Special Courts take direct cognizance without prior approval.

s: How did the 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act treat economic boycott and social boycott?
o: Left to the Protection of Civil Rights Act
x: The 2015 amendment defined economic and social boycott and made them offences amounting to atrocities.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Dedicating a woman as a devadasi was made an atrocity
Special Courts may take direct cognizance
Trial is to be completed within 90 days of the charge-sheet
x: The 2015 amendment set the trial to be completed within 60 days of the charge-sheet, not 90.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2015 amendment to the Atrocities Act:
1. Abusing by caste name was made an atrocity.
2. Garlanding with footwear was made an atrocity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are among the new atrocities added in 2015, along with tonsuring, witchcraft accusations and forced manual scavenging.

s: In which year did the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 come into force?
x: The PoA Amendment Act, 2015 came into force in 2016.

s: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act was enacted in which year?
x: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act was passed in 2018, restoring safeguards after a Supreme Court ruling. The Protection of Civil Rights Act dates from 1955.

s: Which of the following cases is associated with the Supreme Court directions that were perceived as diluting the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
x: In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra, decided on 20 March 2018, the Supreme Court issued directions concerning preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court decide Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India?
x: Prithvi Raj Chauhan came in February 2020, after the Mahajan judgment (2018) and its recall (2019).

s: What did the Supreme Court do in Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain (2025)?
o: Declared Section 18 of the Atrocities Act unconstitutional.
Directed that a preliminary enquiry must precede every arrest.
Cancelled an anticipatory bail granted by a High Court and held that no mini-trial should be conducted at the bail stage.
Upheld anticipatory bail despite the existence of a prima facie case.
x: The Supreme Court cancelled the High Court's anticipatory bail, held that Section 18 applies where a prima facie case exists and stated that a mini-trial is impermissible at the bail stage.

s: In Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India, when did the Supreme Court say courts may quash proceedings under the Atrocities Act?
o: The accused is a public servant
A DSP has made a preliminary enquiry
x: Chauhan upheld the 2018 amendment; relief or quashing is available only where no prima facie case exists.

s: When were the Subhash Kashinath Mahajan directions of March 2018 recalled on review?
x: The Mahajan directions were recalled on review in October 2019.

s: Which Section was inserted by the 2018 amendment to the Atrocities Act in response to the Mahajan judgment?
x: The 2018 Amendment Act inserted Section 18A (no preliminary enquiry or approval before arrest), not Section 4A.

s: In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan (2018), the Supreme Court required a preliminary enquiry before registering an FIR by an officer of which rank?
x: Mahajan required a preliminary enquiry by a DSP, a direction later recalled; Section 18A now bars it.

s: Whose rehabilitation does the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 provide for?
x: The AP Devadasis Act 1989 is for the rehabilitation of Jogin women.

s: By how much did crimes against Scheduled Tribes decline as per NCRB data for 2024?
x: Crimes against STs fell by 23.1% and against SCs by 3.6%.

s: Where is Andhra Pradesh's Exclusive Court for SC/ST atrocity cases located?
x: AP has 14 Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Laxmipet, Srikakulam, with an SOP involving Police, Revenue, Judiciary and Welfare.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 is primarily associated with prohibition of which practice?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 was enacted against the Jogini system.

s: What was the conviction rate under the PoA Act in 2022?
x: The PoA conviction rate fell to about 32-33% in 2022 from 39-40% in 2020, with pendency near 97%.

s: Which State recorded the most crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2023?
x: Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh were the top States in 2023.

s: Which district had the most atrocity-prone villages in Andhra Pradesh as per the MHA list of July 2022?
x: Of AP's 53 atrocity-prone villages, East Godavari had 47, Kadapa 5 and Srikakulam 1.

s: Besides one Exclusive Court, how many Special Sessions Courts does Andhra Pradesh have for SC/ST atrocity cases?
x: AP has 14 Special Sessions Courts and 1 Exclusive Court at Laxmipet, Srikakulam.

s: As per NCRB data for 2024, how many crimes against Scheduled Castes were recorded in India?
x: NCRB 2024 recorded 55,698 crimes against SCs, 3.6% fewer than 57,789 in 2023.

s: How many atrocity-prone villages did the MHA identify in Andhra Pradesh in July 2022?
x: MHA listed 53 atrocity-prone villages in AP: East Godavari 47, Kadapa 5 and Srikakulam 1.
